document.text:
In a competitive market, buyers create demand and sellers create supply. The market price coordinates their plans. When the price rises, buyers usually demand a smaller quantity, while sellers usually supply a larger quantity. When the price falls, those responses reverse.

If quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, a shortage puts upward pressure on price. The higher price decreases quantity demanded and increases quantity supplied until the shortage narrows. If quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, a surplus puts downward pressure on price.

Price elasticity measures how strongly quantity responds to a price change. When demand is less elastic, a similar reduction in supply can cause a larger price increase because buyers reduce their quantity demanded by less.

entities.description: The quantity buyers demand at a given price.

entities.name: quantity supplied
entities.description: The quantity sellers supply at a given price.

entities.name: shortage
entities.description: A market condition in which quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

entities.name: surplus
entities.description: A market condition in which quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.

entities.name: upward pressure on price
entities.description: Pressure produced by a shortage that pushes the market price upward.

entities.name: downward pressure on price
entities.description: Pressure produced by a surplus that pushes the market price downward.

entities.name: buyers
entities.description: Market participants that create demand and respond to price changes through quantity demanded.

entities.name: sellers
entities.description: Market participants that create supply and respond to price changes through quantity supplied.

entities.name: demand elasticity
entities.description: A measure of how strongly quantity demanded responds to a price change.

entities.name: reduction in supply
entities.description: A decrease in supply that can produce a price increase, with the effect depending on demand elasticity.
